Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you have a pruritic rash on your trunk and extremities, along with a recent history of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. To better understand your condition, have you noticed any specific pattern to the rash, such as it appearing in crops or being itchy at night?

REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC) with differential.
REQUEST IMAGES: Please provide any photographs of the rash you may have taken.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: COMPLETE BLOOD COUNT: WBC Normal, Hemoglobin Normal, Platelets Slightly elevated. SKIN EXAMINATION: Lacy, reticular rash noted on the trunk and extremities. Facial rash present but sparing the perioral area. Rash is slightly raised but not accompanied by significant warmth or tenderness. VITAL SIGNS: Temperature 37.4°C (99.3°F), Blood Pressure 100/70 mmHg, Heart Rate 80 bpm, Respiratory Rate 18 breaths/min. THROAT CULTURE: Negative for Group A Streptococcus. NOTE: No photographs of the rash were provided in the current dataset.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease). The clinical picture of a pruritic, lacy reticular rash on the trunk and extremities, combined with a "slapped cheek" appearance (rash sparing the perioral area) and recent viral prodrome symptoms like rhinorrhea and low-grade fever, is classic for Parvovirus B19 infection. The normal white blood cell count and negative throat culture further support a viral etiology rather than a bacterial one.
